verdict.rationale: Steel documents a Sessions API for spinning up isolated browser instances on demand, with programmatic lifecycle control (create with custom IDs), and markets itself as controlling "fleets of browsers in the cloud." However, nothing in the evidence documents concurrency limits or explicitly describes running many sessions in parallel. missing for 10: documented concurrency limits or quotas per plan, explicit concurrent/parallel session documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration of fleet-scale operation.

support.subject: As an automation-engineer, I can run a fleet of concurrent browser sessions with documented concurrency limits and programmatic session management

citations.quote: the Sessions API lets your agents spin up isolated browser instances on demand. Each session maintains its own state, cookies, and storage
Steel is an open source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
Steel generates a session ID for you, but `create` also accepts one. Pass your own UUID when the ID has to exist before the browser does
